subject: physiology
title: Plasma proteins, red cells and haemoglobin: core physiology for NEET-PG and USMLE

steps.tx: Plasma proteins are mostly made by the liver. **Albumin** is the most abundant and it is the main contributor to **colloid osmotic (oncotic) pressure**, which holds water in the circulation. Oncotic pressure depends on the number of molecules, not their mass. Albumin has a low molecular weight and high concentration, so it contributes most. Normal plasma oncotic pressure is about 28 mm Hg.

steps.tx: Red cells are biconcave discs. This shape gives a **large surface area to volume ratio**, which speeds gas exchange. The shape also lets the cell squeeze through small capillaries and change volume without rupturing. The membrane skeleton, made of **spectrin**, **ankyrin** and **band 3**, gives flexibility. Defects in these proteins cause spherocytosis.

vis.alt: Biconcave red cell in cross-section with diameter about 7.5 micrometres, and a haemoglobin molecule of two alpha and two beta chains each with a haem iron; adult HbA is alpha two beta two, HbF alpha two gamma two, HbA2 alpha two delta two.
vis.caption: Biconcave shape gives a high surface to volume ratio and flexibility; HbA is two alpha and two beta chains, each with one haem.

steps.tx: Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein. In adults about 85 percent comes from the **kidney**, from interstitial cells of the peritubular capillary bed, and about 15 percent from the liver. The only key physiological stimulus is **hypoxia**, meaning low tissue oxygen tension. Fetal erythropoietin is made in the liver in early gestation and shifts to the kidney after birth.

steps.tx: Erythropoiesis shifts sites with age. In the yolk sac first, then the **liver** and spleen in mid-gestation, then **red bone marrow** from late gestation onward. After about 20 years, marrow in long bones becomes fatty and red production shifts to flat bones such as vertebrae, sternum, ribs and ilia. A normal erythroid cycle takes about 7 days in marrow.

steps.tx: Fetal haemoglobin, **HbF** (alpha2 gamma2), has a higher oxygen affinity than adult HbA. The reason is that HbF binds **2,3-DPG** poorly, not that DPG levels are low. The curve is therefore shifted left. Switchover from fetal to adult synthesis begins around 36 weeks of gestation. Normal adult HbA2 is alpha2 delta2 and is about 2.5 percent of total haemoglobin.
